content.text: I'll start by gathering telemetry data, knowledge base entries, and service history in parallel since these are independent investigations.

The telemetry shows a clear, sustained trend: coolant temp rising steadily from ~90°C to 114°C over an hour, while coolant level dropped in lockstep from 96% to 76%. This matches KB-002 (sustained spike correlated with low coolant level, indicating real leak/coolant loss) rather than KB-001 (transient sensor glitch with no real coolant loss, which would show stable coolant level). Oil pressure and RPM stayed normal/stable, ruling out broader engine failure but not contradicting a coolant leak.

input.description: KB-001 and KB-002 disagree: KB-001 attributes coolant spikes to a transient sensor glitch (no real temp rise), while KB-002 attributes sustained spikes with falling coolant level to an actual leak requiring service. Telemetry shows coolant_temp_c climbing steadily from 90°C to 114°C over 60 minutes while coolant_level_pct dropped in parallel from 96% to 76% -- a strong, monotonic correlation, not a transient blip. This matches KB-002's pattern, not KB-001's. Oil pressure and RPM remained stable, so this appears isolated to coolant loss. Recommend scheduling a physical service visit to inspect for a coolant leak rather than restarting the sensor.
